extraction: Film data extracted from user-supplied horror-globe.html without executing page scripts. In v17.5, the original Natural Earth vector-map raster was replaced by the NASA satellite composite described under earth_texture. Film and location content remains unchanged.
film_content_verification: User-supplied film/location/visiting content retained; not independently fact-checked. Visiting status is source content, not current travel guidance.
poster_fields: All 200 source poster fields are blank. bookCover uses the existing library asset only for exact title + year matches.
map_detail: 4096×2048 downsample of NASA’s genuine 5400×2700 September 2004 Blue Marble: Next Generation global image. No upscaling or synthetic detail.
map_style: Natural-color cloudless satellite composite: land vegetation, deserts, coastlines, Greenland and Antarctic ice; deep ocean is NASA’s uniform navy fill. No added boundaries, graticule, cloud layers, tinting, repainting, or AI processing.
sphere_uv: Three SphereGeometry; x=cos(latitude)*cos(longitude), y=sin(latitude), z=-cos(latitude)*sin(longitude). Texture x=(longitude+180)/360; y=(90-latitude)/180.

earth_texture.title: Blue Marble: Next Generation — September 2004, Base Map
earth_texture.producer: Reto Stöckli, NASA Earth Observatory (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center)
earth_texture.source_resolution_note: NASA labels this global download 5400×2700, 8km/pixel. It is a monthly satellite-data composite, not current/live imagery or street-level photography.
earth_texture.usage_note: NASA publishes these texture/media assets for use under its media guidelines and requests acknowledgment. This globe credits NASA Earth Observatory and does not imply NASA endorsement. No NASA logo is used.
processing: Lanczos downsample directly from original to each output size
Encode lossy WebP at the recorded quality and method
earth_texture.color_space: RGB diffuse texture for sRGB sampling. Source JPEG has no embedded ICC profile; no color transform was applied.
earth_texture.uv_orientation: Image x=(longitude+180)/360 and y=(90-latitude)/180. North is at top and ±180° seam is at the edges. Three SphereGeometry default UV and texture flipY=true match existing pins x=cos(lat)*cos(lon), y=sin(lat), z=-cos(lat)*sin(lon). No asset or pin orientation change required.
earth_texture.validation: Visually compared old and new maps. Verified export dimensions, format and byte budgets; inspected six geographically distributed landmark pixels using the unchanged latitude/longitude mapping.

render_treatment_v17_6.request: Keep the globe ocean visibly blue throughout rotation, independent of the room lights.
render_treatment_v17_6.scope: Globe-only material treatment at rendering time. NASA source and all WebP texture files remain unchanged.
render_treatment_v17_6.method: Identify dark blue-dominant ocean texels and lift their surface and emitted blue color. Preserve original vegetation, desert, and ice color. Keep a nonzero self-lit baseline through the existing pulse.
render_treatment_v17_6.resolution: No resampling, image generation, or new detail. Original NASA and v17.5 texture sizes and hashes are unchanged.

render_treatment_v17_9.request: Earth-from-space appearance based on the user reference, retaining working location pins and zoom.
render_treatment_v17_9.clouds: Separate historical NASA Blue Marble cloud coverage overlay; see globe-clouds-PROVENANCE.json. It is not live weather.
render_treatment_v17_9.method: One cloud mask sample reused by diffuse and emissive shading, slow cloud drift and a view-dependent blue atmospheric rim in the existing sphere material. No extra renderer, sphere mesh or fullscreen bloom pass.
render_treatment_v17_9.loading: Cloud mask loads only when the globe is approached/opened, with 2048 desktop and 1024 mobile/save-data texture tiers. Failure leaves the satellite globe usable.
render_treatment_v17_9.source_preservation: Existing NASA land/ocean source and three exports, UV geographic mapping, and location coordinates are unchanged.

render_treatment_v17_10.ocean: Saturated deep navy/cobalt, always illuminated, with stronger neutral directional form shading
render_treatment_v17_10.atmosphere: Texture-free additive BackSide shell with a soft outer fade and shared glow pulse
render_treatment_v17_10.pins: One instanced tapered-needle draw, point at radius1.045 and marker at1.19; existing NASA UV coordinates unchanged
render_treatment_v17_10.lift: Rest center1.49, raised center3.0; full globe visible above tabletop in Locations and near/focused360 viewing
render_treatment_v17_10.sources: Same existing NASA Earth and cloud files; no new image generation or image downloads
